st: Put the potatoes in a pot of cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook for 15 minutes until tender. Drain.
In another pot, add the cod to simmering salted water. Cook gently for 5 minutes until it flakes.
Lift out the fish, drain well, and flake it into chunks, removing any bones.
Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft but not brown.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the warm milk to make a smooth white sauce.
Simmer the sauce for 3 minutes until thick, then season with [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Fold in the potatoes, breaking them up a little, and then the fish. Heat gently for 5 minutes. It should be chunky, not smooth.
Top with chives and serve with buttered dark rye bread.
Put the lamb in a large pot with the water. Bring slowly to a boil.
Skim off the foam that rises to the top for the first 10 minutes.
Add the onion, rice, salt, pepper and thyme. Cover and simmer on low for 1 hour.
Add the carrots and rutabaga and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 15 minutes more until all the vegetables are soft.
Lift the lamb out and remove the meat from the bones. Cut it into bite-size pieces and return it to the soup.
Stir in the parsley and taste. Add more salt if needed.
Serve hot in big bowls with dark rye bread.
Place the smoked lamb in a large pot and cover with cold water. If it is very salty, soak it in cold water for 1 hour first.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 1.5 to 2 hours, about 30 minutes per pound, until tender and 160°F (71°C) inside.
About 20 minutes before the lamb is done, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain.
Melt the butter in a pan and whisk in the flour. Cook for 1 minute.
Slowly add the warm milk, whisking, and simmer for 5 minutes until thick.
Stir in the sugar, nutmeg and pepper. Taste for salt, though the meat will be salty.
Heat the peas in simmering water for 3 minutes and drain.
Rest the lamb for 10 minutes, slice it, and serve with the potatoes, peas and white sauce.

ing: with live cultures, as a starter, or plain Greek yogurt
st: Heat the milk in a large pot to 185°F (85°C), stirring so it does not scorch, and hold it there for 10 minutes.
Cool the milk to 100°F (38°C) by setting the pot in a sink of cold water.
Whisk the starter into a ladle of the warm milk, then stir it back into the pot.
Add the rennet diluted in a spoonful of cool water and stir gently.
Cover the pot, wrap in a towel, and keep warm for 6 to 8 hours until set like a soft yogurt.
Line a colander with cheesecloth. Pour in the set milk and let it drain in the fridge for 4 to 6 hours until very thick.
Stir the thick skyr until smooth. Thin with a little cream if you like.
Serve in bowls with the cream, sugar and blueberries.
Heat the oven to 250°F (120°C). Grease a loaf pan or lidded baking tin with the butter.
Mix the rye flour, all-purpose flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt in a large bowl.
Stir the molasses into the buttermilk and milk until dissolved.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir until just combined. The batter will be thick and sticky.
Scrape into the pan and cover very tightly with a lid or foil, so it can steam.
Bake for 5 hours at low heat until firm, dark and moist.
Cool completely in the pan, then take it out and wrap.
Slice thickly and serve with butter and smoked fish or lamb.
Bring the water to a gentle simmer in a pot. Do not let it boil hard.
Add the hot dogs and heat for 5 minutes until hot all the way through.
Lightly steam or warm the buns in the microwave for 15 seconds, or on a tray in a low oven.
Open each bun and set a hot dog in it.
Squeeze [[1 tbsp]] ketchup in a line along each hot dog, then [[1 tbsp]] mustard.
Add [[1 tbsp]] remoulade to each.
Sprinkle with the raw chopped onion and then the crispy fried onions.
Serve right away, so the buns stay soft and the onions crunchy.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom and salt in a large bowl.
Beat the eggs with the buttermilk and butter, then pour into the dry ingredients.
Mix gently into a soft dough, adding a spoon of flour if too sticky. Chill, covered, for 30 minutes.
Roll out on a floured surface to about 1/2 inch thick. Cut into rectangles about 1 by 3 inches.
Cut a slit in the center of each piece and pull one end through the slit to make a twist.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the kleinur a few at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and cool. Dust with sugar if you like.
Mix the rye flour, all-purpose flour, baking soda, salt and sugar in a bowl.
Pour in the hot milk and stir until a stiff dough forms. Add a splash more if it is too dry.
Knead for 2 minutes until smooth. Divide into 8 balls.
Roll each ball very thin into a round about 6 inches wide, using flour. Prick all over with a fork.
Heat a dry cast iron pan over medium-high heat.
Cook each flatbread for 1 to 2 minutes per side until dark brown spots appear. Do not add any oil.
Stack them wrapped in a towel to keep soft.
Spread with butter and fold, or top with the smoked lamb.
Take the dried fish from the pack. It is hard and leathery, which is normal.
Lay the fish on a board and beat it with a rolling pin or meat mallet for 3 minutes to tenderize and loosen it.
Tear the fish into bite-size strips along the grain, removing any bones or skin.
Soften the butter and, if using, mix in the garlic.
Spread the butter on the slices of rye bread.
Cut the bread into pieces. Sprinkle with flaky salt if you like.
Serve the fish strips with the buttered bread, spreading a layer of butter on each piece of fish before eating.

ing: melted, plus more for the pan
st: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and cinnamon in a bowl.
In another bowl, beat the eggs with half the milk, the vanilla and the melted butter.
Pour into the dry mix and whisk smooth. Add the rest of the milk until the batter is thin like cream.
Rest the batter for 15 minutes.
Heat a wide nonstick pan or crepe pan over medium heat and brush with a little butter.
Pour in about [[0.25 cup]] batter and tilt the pan so it spreads very thin.
Cook for 1 minute until the edges lift, flip, and cook for 30 seconds more.
Sprinkle with sugar, roll up or fold in quarters, and serve warm with cream if you like.
